reported.title: Serial output uses wrong prefix, so no Temp line ever matches
reported.description: printTemp() at line 34 emits the literal "temp=" instead of the required "Temp: " prefix, so the printed line never matches the expected format. The measured evidence confirms this: "No serial line matched /^Temp: -?[0-9]+\.[0-9]$/ in 8.00 s" across all scenarios including the nominal ramp. The one-decimal formatting on line 35 is correct, but the label is wrong. No serial line matched /^Temp: -?[0-9]+\.[0-9]$/ in 8.00 s; expected one every 1000 ms.

reported.title: Temperature value cannot be parsed because of the wrong serial prefix
reported.description: Because printTemp() at line 34 prints "temp=" rather than "Temp: ", the value regex /Temp: (-?[0-9.]+)/ never matches, so the reported temperature can never be compared to the probe. The measured evidence states "No serial line matched /Temp: (-?[0-9.]+)/ so the printed value could not be compared with A0" in every scenario. The underlying conversion on line 23 is not the cause here; the output label on line 34 is. No serial line matched /Temp: (-?[0-9.]+)/ so the printed value could not be compared with A0.

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial lines matching '^Temp: ' every 1000 ms (Temp: lines)
serial values for 'Temp: (-?[0-9.]+)' match the stimulus (tolerance 1.5) (Value OK)

judge_input.spec:
- TMP36 on A0 (10 mV/°C with 500 mV offset); freeze button on D5 (pull-up); range lamp on D7.
- Every 1000 ms print exactly `Temp: <celsius>` with a space after the colon and one decimal place.
- Printed temperature must stay within ±1.5 °C of the injected probe value.
- While D5 is held LOW, freeze the reported value at the last sample.
- Light D7 when the reported temperature is outside -10.0 to 50.0 °C.
- Also print `weather n=<samples>` each second after the Temp line.

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial lines matching '^Temp: ' every 1000 ms (Temp: lines)
serial values for 'Temp: (-?[0-9.]+)' match the stimulus (tolerance 1.5) (Value OK)
